schema.title: Workflow delayed continuation ownership and verification

rearming_pattern.cancel_action: The business Action clears <date-or-datetime-field> when the governing state no longer needs a continuation.
rearming_pattern.due_action: Re-read the governing business state and produce no effect when the timer is stale; otherwise apply the idempotent due effect and persist the next exact due instant when recurrence-by-rearming is required.
rearming_pattern.schedule_action: The business Action computes and persists the exact next due instant in <date-or-datetime-field>.
rearming_pattern.timer_rule: The timer_from_record_field node consumes source_field only; it does not recalculate an already-final business due instant.

selection.timer_from_record_field: Resume from an exact date or datetime field common to every trigger Object. When the business Action already calculated the final instant, do not add offset_seconds or business_calendar_key.
selection.wait_duration: Resume after a positive elapsed duration.
selection.wait_until: Resume at one fixed RFC3339 instant.

x-domainry-forbidden: a verification-only clock or time input on a production Workflow or Action
a business Action or Workflow added only to make a short verification due authorable
claiming a timer observation or Runtime timer integration certificate that was not independently produced and identity-checked
a tenant Scheduler definition for one delayed continuation
a startup fixture or bootstrap mutation that fabricates elapsed time
a browser timer or project cron daemon as the time owner

delayed_continuation.author: A timer, wait_until, or wait_duration node in the Workflow graph.
delayed_continuation.intent: Pause one already-started Workflow execution once and resume that same execution when its due time arrives.

recurrence.author: A scheduled_jobs definition targeting a scheduled Workflow or report snapshot refresh.
recurrence.intent: Start a distinct governed run for each repeated calendar or interval window.

x-domainry-runtime-persistence.resume: The due timer is claimed with fencing and resumes the existing Workflow process through its ordinary durable continuation path.

x-domainry-verification.evidence_binding: The compiled manifest and immutable implementation packet bind the production Action/Workflow identities, focused Handler test paths, and exact Runtime timer integration certificate identity. A missing certificate or observation leaves verification incomplete.
required_observations: the production Action black-box path computes and persists the requirement's real due value and does not produce the due business effect immediately

when the accepted business surface already permits a short future due, one same-business black-box case observes record_timer.due_at, no effect before due, and the same Workflow process advancing after due
when that short due is not legally authorable, project Handler focused tests use a dependency-injected clock to prove pre-due and due business semantics without exposing time through production input
when that short due is not legally authorable, an independently produced Runtime timer integration certificate proves record_timer pre-due, due claim/fencing/resume, and restart mechanics
the compiled manifest and immutable implementation packet bind every selected evidence identity, and stale, retry, or restart paths do not create a duplicate business effect
x-domainry-verification.strategy: Use a short real future due and bounded black-box polling only when the accepted business surface already permits that due value. Otherwise combine production-Action black-box proof, focused Handler tests with a dependency-injected clock, and an independently produced Runtime timer integration certificate; do not widen the business surface or add a Runtime clock seam.
